title: Chapter 144: We Are All Monsters (1)
html:
After lunch, Chen Ge returned to the staff break room and found Xu Wan crouching beside the door. “What are you doing?”

“Boss, when did you get a cat? She’s beautiful, but she won’t let me touch her.” Xu Wan pouted. “I only want a hug.”

“Forget it. She’s a stray and distrusts people.” Chen Ge entered and replaced the boards. The cat did not hiss at him, but still moved away to avoid physical contact.

“Then why isn’t the cat hostile toward you?” Xu Wan was confused. Whenever she neared the cat, it would assume a hostile posture.

“Perhaps she recognizes that I’m trustworthy and noble.” Chen Ge sat on the bed and stretched. “Do you want to rest?”

“I’m fine. Take a nap; I’ll wake you at 1:15 p.m.” Xu Wan gazed at the white cat. “What is her name?”

“I tried several, but she hated them all. She responded to White Tiger, so I may keep that.” Chen Ge regarded the cat seriously.

“You want to call a cat White Tiger?” Xu Wan thought that Chen Ge was kidding with her, but he didn’t look like it. “Well, as long as you’re happy.”

After Xu Wan left, Chen Ge studied the cat. She could see supernatural entities, and even Xiaoxiao, a Baleful Specter, feared her. If trained, she could become a powerful trump card. But she was a living creature with a will of her own, and earning obedience would take time. At least one night together had softened her hostility. She was clever enough to distinguish friend from foe.

“Your kittens are gone. Guarding them cannot change that.” After a moment, Chen Ge picked up the basket. The white cat followed him outside.

He dug a grave beneath a tall tree and placed the kittens inside, watching their mother in case grief drove her to attack.

“I understand your pain and how important they are, but…” Crouching, Chen Ge slowly filled the grave. “Everything dies and returns to nature. Only through burial can their souls reenter the Great Cycle.”

Whether she understood or not, the cat watched the mound. Her mismatched eyes trembled as the four kittens disappeared from sight, but she neither attacked nor lost control. She simply sat in silence.

When Chen Ge scattered the final handful of earth, she retreated into a hollow in the tree and ignored every attempt to coax her out. As lunch ended and visitors returned, she emerged only to climb higher into the branches.

Chen Ge could not force the cat to do something it did not want to, so after a quick cleaning, he opened the Haunted House for business.

With a new Two-Star Scenario waiting, many visitors immediately queued again after completing Murder by Midnight or Minghun. The tier system was already working: restrictions only heightened their curiosity, and thrill seekers found the unknown scenario irresistible.

Chen Ge worked until closing, then followed Uncle Xu to collect the surveillance equipment. After sending Xu Wan and Uncle Xu home, he entered Mu Yang High School alone and installed cameras at several key points.

Installation took longer than expected, and he finished at 8:00 p.m. After washing, he called Doctor Gao and Wang Hailong, then took a taxi to Hai Ming Apartments. Both men were waiting when he arrived.

Doctor Gao’s calm manner and psychological expertise quickly won over the Wang brothers. By the time Chen Ge arrived, they were already chatting comfortably.

“My dad and Shenglong live on the sixth floor. I’ve informed them of our visit this afternoon.”

As they entered Hai Ming Apartments, Chen Ge frowned. The peculiar stench had returned, strongest on the third floor, yet neither companion reacted. They continued discussing Wang Shenglong.

What is the source of this smell?

He had blamed the animal carcasses in Room 302, but those should be gone. Why did the odor remain?

On the top floor, Wang Hailong knocked on Room 601. A deeply frowning man in his fifties answered, his hair already salt-and-pepper.

“Dad, this is the Haunted House boss who experienced something similar, and this is the best psychologist in Jiujiang.”

“Please, come in.”

Everyday belongings crowded the apartment, which felt cramped with so many visitors.

“I understand why you came. Shenglong is in the bedroom. Cure him, and you’ll never worry about money again.” Worry had aged the father far beyond his years.

“May we meet him?” Chen Ge stood at the back. When the bedroom opened, the stench struck him like a wall, yet no one else reacted. Apparently, he alone could smell it.

“Okay, but I hope you are mentally prepared.” Wang Shenglong’s father pushed the bedroom door open.

A stronger odor flowed out, and Chen Ge discreetly touched a finger beneath his nose. It was not foul so much as viscerally repellent, triggering an instinct to flee. The scent seemed to whisper, “Do not approach. This thing is dangerous.”

The small bedroom held no furniture, only a thin carpet and several pillows in the corners. At its center sat a man.

Barely 1.5 meters tall and severely overweight, he had legs deformed beneath his own weight and a nearly spherical body.

At the sight of visitors, he smiled innocently and laboriously lifted one hand in greeting.

Every stranger’s first reaction cut Wang Shenglong’s father like a knife. “Shenglong cannot speak, but his other faculties are normal. Ask a question, and he’ll answer on the board.”
